verdict.rationale: AutoGen's core interaction model is natural-language: users define tasks/messages for AssistantAgent (LLM-driven) and provide feedback via UserProxyAgent, and AutoGen Studio lets users specify agent teams declaratively or via drag-and-drop rather than code. However, the evidence never explicitly frames the whole product as controllable via natural-language 'commands' (e.g., a chat-based control plane or NL-to-action mapping for configuring/running the framework itself), and community notes point to inconsistent quality of agent-to-agent NL exchanges rather than confirming a smooth NL command interface for the user. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of natural-language driven configuration/control of the framework, independent hands-on evidence confirming reliable NL command execution.
